title: Consolidate worker lease semantics and centralize retry/backpressure orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem summary: Our fleet of async consumers (Redis lease-based and Kafka consumer groups) exhibits noisy failure modes under transient load: short Redis lease TTLs plus jitterless exponential retry cause duplicate work and thundering requeues; Kafka consumer retries are implemented ad-hoc in multiple services leading to inconsistent offset handling; busy-looping when downstream is saturated increases CPU and makes P95 latency spike. Root causes: inconsistent lease/visibility semantics across services, no unified retry policy (max attempts/jitter/backoff profiles), and absence of a global backpressure token mechanism to shed load gracefully. Goal: refactor worker lease management into a shared library and introduce a centralized retry-and-backpressure coordinator that normalizes retry semantics, exposes metrics, and supports gradual rollout via feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: Library deployed and consumed by at least 3 critical services (ingest, routing, embeddings-consumer)
Redis-based leases use renew-on-claim semantics with TTL >= processing p99 + slop and demonstrate <1% duplicate deliveries in controlled replay tests
Kafka consumers move to consistent in-process retry wrapper that preserves at-least-once semantics but avoids immediate re-poll busy loops
A token-bucket backpressure controller is exposed with prom metrics and a single boolean feature flag per service to opt-in/out
End-to-end benchmark shows 30% reduction in CPU during overload and P95 token generation latency improvement of >=15%
Migration documented with rollback steps and smoke tests; no customer-facing regression after canary rollout to staging and 10% of prod traffic
implementation_notes: Introduce new package runtime/workerlib that implements: LeaseManager (renew, extend, heartbeat), RetryPolicy (configurable attempts, base/backoff, jitter), BackpressureController (token-bucket with dynamic fill rate)
LeaseManager will standardize Redis key format: rl:leases:<queue>:<worker_id> and use server-side Lua for safe check-and-extend operations

Kafka consumer changes: replace per-service ad-hoc retry with a shared consumer wrapper that moves failed messages to a local retry queue with exponential+full-jitter and respects consumer pause/resume APIs to avoid busy polling
Expose metrics: workerlib.lease_renew_success, workerlib.lease_collision, workerlib.retry_attempts_total, workerlib.backpressure_tokens, and histograms for hold times
Feature flags: runtime.features.workerlib_v1 (boolean) to allow gradual opt-in; runtime.features.bp_controller (boolean) for backpressure on/off
Compatibility: Provide shim adapter for older services to call into runtime/workerlib with minimal code changes; keep previous Redis client until migration complete
Use server-side Redis scripts to ensure atomic lease renewals and avoid race conditions observed in previous incidents
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Merge library and tests behind feature flags (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1534)
Phase 1: Canary deploy to staging clusters, run synthetic replay workload for 48h (compare duplicates and CPU) (Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-25678+Design)
Phase 2: Opt-in ingest service (10% traffic) + monitor for 72h; if stable, increment to 50%
Phase 3: Backfill other consumers (routing, embeddings) and enable backpressure controller in read-only mode to collect metrics, then enable enforcement
Phase 4: Full rollout and deprecation of legacy retry codepaths; schedule technical debt cleanup ticket to remove shims (ENG-XXXXX)
testing_plan: Unit tests for LeaseManager Lua scripts and edge cases (lease collision, expired extend)
Integration tests: end-to-end Kafka consumer with local retry queue and pause/resume behavior under backpressure
Chaos tests: introduce Redis latency/partition in staging and assert no duplicate processing >2% over 1M messages
Load tests: synthetic 5x traffic spike to validate token-bucket shedding and CPU delta metrics
Performance benchmarks recorded in GH actions and linked in PR description
comments: 2026-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Created initial spike and prototype for LeaseManager. Prototype uses redis.lua extend script; saw race when two workers attempt extend at same millisecond.

2026-02-19 - Marco Rivera: Implemented server-side Lua CAS for lease extend; pushed draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1519. Noted trade-off: slightly higher Redis CPU for atomic operations but eliminates duplicate deliveries under contention.

2026-02-26 - QA (Lena Kim): Ran replay test with 200k messages, duplicate rate dropped from 4.6% to 0.8% when LeaseManager was used. Observed higher Redis CPU by ~8% — acceptable with smaller TTL and batching optimizations.
2026-03-03 - Infra (Jonas Müller): Raised concern about single Redis namespace write amplification; recommended adding rate-limited batching and TTL heuristics. Added as follow-up task.

2026-03-08 - Design review: Decided to use full jitter for retry backoff to avoid synchronization (ref: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/exponential-backoff-and-jitter/). Documented in Confluence.

2026-03-10 - Marco Rivera: Implemented BackpressureController prototype and integrated with ingest service via feature flag. Initial canary (staging) showed 32% CPU reduction under overload. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1534
2026-03-12 - Product (Sara Lin): Verified no SLO regressions on user-facing endpoints in canary; signed off to progress to 10% prod traffic
2026-03-13 - Marco Rivera: Opened monitoring dashboards (Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/workerlib/workerlib-overview) and alert rules (alert: WorkerLibHighDuplicateRate)
2026-03-14 - Aisha Patel: Updating ticket with next steps: expand canary, schedule post-rollout audit, and cut follow-up tickets for Redis namespace batching and documentation cleanup
